definitions.explanation: Shoes made of leather, typically formal or business-style footwear. A standard part of business attire in Japan.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧{革靴|かわぐつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
{革靴|かわぐつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{濡|ぬ}れて→濡れる：00800_nureru⟧しまった。
examples.english: My leather shoes got wet in the rain.

examples.japanese: ⟦{面接|めんせつ}→面接：01100_mensetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前日|ぜんじつ}→前日：03108_zenjitsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{革靴|かわぐつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{磨|みが}いて→磨く：02427_migaku⟧、⟦{準備|じゅんび}→準備：01431_junbi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{整|ととの}えた→整える：04259_totonoeru⟧。
examples.english: The day before the interview, I polished my leather shoes and got everything ready.

notes:
USAGE:
{革靴|かわぐつ} is standard vocabulary for business and formal contexts in Japan. New employees typically purchase {革靴|かわぐつ} as part of their business attire.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {革靴|かわぐつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{磨|みが}く→磨く：02427_migaku⟧ (to polish leather shoes)
- {革靴|かわぐつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧ (to wear leather shoes)
- {革靴|かわぐつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{手入|てい}れ→手入れ：07178_teire⟧ (leather shoe care)
